reason: All clauses (a)-(f) are present for the specified independent uniform-unit model: bounds, population moments, almost-sure rank, conditional nonlinearity, zero conditional meats, exact nonzero score covariance, positive leading limit, Gaussian coefficient limit, sandwich consistency, and singleton/unit-weight extensions. Definitions are ordinary projection, covariance, product sampling and ordered overlap sums.

The single-record identities (i)-(v), full conditional covariance decomposition and disjoint remainder are present. The repeated/weighted prescription allows dyad- and record-dependent bounded functions, deterministic positive finite counts, fixed real weights, and exactly the relevant nonsingular expected Gram; it includes the centering products, the iff cancellation criterion, and the stated normalizations. The Unit witness is within these explicit hypotheses.

The fair-sign model, exact fitted meat and moments, raw and normalized mean discrepancies, missing-N deterministic sequence, fourth/linear-product moments, actual fitted-residual covariances, spike sequence, and all-N>=3 inverse-Gram counterexample and infinite extended norm expectation are present. The operator norm definition has a nonempty bounded supremum set. The examples do not assert failure of consistency.

The unconditional absolute consistency statement under S9 is present. Generic square-integrable Z in the finite Chebyshev bound and sequence criterion specializes to Z_N=N*Vhat, giving exactly the corrected scaling. It imposes no inverse-Gram or sandwich moment requirement on the consistency result. Equivalent finite-dimensional norms and the permitted zero completion on singular samples do not change the convergence claim.

Retains the N=3 incidence/covariance matrices and universal parameter mismatch, all fixed-component GLS products and the variance ratio, and the abstract translation-equivariant variance decomposition/lower bound. Omits the random-effect covariance derivations, general-N mismatch and count, Gaussian average/centered-effect independence and its link to design (4), four numeric bounds, and repeated extension. Independence of yc from the Gaussian average and both estimator second moments are explicit antecedents instead of being derived for the simulation design.
